claim: Number embeddings are periodic with periods 2, 5, 10
published: Fourier peaks at T = 2, 5, 10 in GPT-J (Kantamneni & Tegmark Fig. 2); 2, 2.5, 5, 10 (Zhou et al. 2024)
criterion: at least two of {2, 5, 10} among the top-4 periods (±5%)

claim: Numbers lie on a generalized helix (T = 2, 5, 10, 100)
published: helix fits the residual stream of GPT-J / Pythia-6.9B / Llama-3.1-8B
ours: pythia-2.8b: 5-fold CV R² over a, max over layers for each basis: helix 0.50 (layer 11) vs -0.11 for a shuffled helix, 0.26 linear-only, 0.38 circles only
criterion: held-out helix R² ≥ 0.5 and ≥ 0.2 above the shuffled control (control fix 2026-11-28: CV, controls max-selected too)

claim: Patching along the helix recovers most of the full-layer effect
published: GPT-J: helix 7.21 vs full 8.34 logit diff (86%); PCA 6.13
ours: pythia-2.8b layer 1: median recovery helix 76%, full layer 100%, PCA-9 80%, linear-only 4% (n = 80 correct prompts; accuracy 85%)
criterion: helix ≥ 50% of the full-layer recovery and ≥ linear-only; full-layer recovery ≥ 50% (m7 guard, 2026-11-28) (needs ≥ 20 correctly solved prompts, else n/a)

claim: Confirmatory: patching along the helix beats generic 9-D subspaces
published: GPT-J: helix 7.21 vs PCA 6.13 logit difference (Kantamneni & Tegmark Table 1)
ours: pythia-2.8b, mean per-prompt recovery, paired differences [95% bootstrap CI]: L1: helix 72% vs random 9-D 2% (diff +70 [+66, +73]) vs PCA-9 78% (diff -6 [-9, -2]); L8: helix 69% vs random 9-D 4% (diff +65 [+62, +68]) vs PCA-9 65% (diff +4 [-1, +9])
criterion: CI > 0 against random 9-D and PCA-9 at every layer with full-layer recovery ≥ 50%; partial if only against random 9-D (pre-stated 2026-11-28)
